units.translation: V. 248 ⟦1⟧ cf. 956. ⟦2⟧. ⟦3⟧, either "who can also kill men" or "who want to kill the man (Orestes)"; when the scholiast explains ⟦4⟧, he seems to regard ⟦5⟧- as a similar intensification as ⟦6⟧- or ⟦7⟧- (⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧). ⟦10⟧ "is roamed through, searched", cf. 196f. and especially 78, where of Or. it is said ⟦11⟧. ⟦12⟧ again oxymoron.

252 ⟦1⟧· ⟦2⟧ Hesych. according to Lobeck's emendation for -⟦3⟧ -⟦4⟧. In ⟦5⟧ the horror of the Erinyes emerges again (likewise several times in what follows): they feast on it. To ⟦6⟧ the metaphor does not fit; but here the harshness is not inappropriate.

254 ff. The first sung pieces are clearly distinguished: ⟦1⟧.. ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧.. ⟦4⟧. ⟦5⟧ like ⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧ (cf. there 876, and see on ⟦8⟧). Further on in M. there stood first probably ⟦9⟧ (⟦10⟧ correction), which is ⟦11⟧; since the demonstrative ⟦12⟧ is so frequent, there is nothing to object to here, and the ⟦13⟧ is to be left with the following verse, from which Hermann removed it to fill out the dochmius: ⟦14⟧. So Sophocles ⟦15⟧: ⟦16⟧.. ⟦17⟧ (⟦18⟧ Herm.), ⟦19⟧, ⟦20⟧ (Weil). ⟦21⟧ (only here) cf. ⟦22⟧ ⟦23⟧, ⟦24⟧, ⟦25⟧ etc. "Whether he has perhaps secretly escaped us". ⟦26⟧ the debtor who does not want to pay, a substantive, to which ⟦27⟧ is an attribute. So Weil; otherwise ⟦28⟧. 7* Epiparodos.
